title: Experts disagree on new change baseline resolver
context:
Chief architect: Ruled by the chief, no question needed: one function owns where the change started, and it also remembers the files that were untracked or dirty when the change opened, because git cannot recover that later. Order: the recorded start point, else the real fork point, else a stated fallback that the HUD names. It never silently diffs against main, since guessing from main is what produced the false counts.

Target: new change baseline resolver
- application-architect: one function owns 'where this change started' (start_commit, else the real fork point, else merge-base with base_branch) and src/hud/changed-files.ts, src/hud/change-scope.ts, src/feature-evidence/delivery.ts commit_split, plan progress, claims and receipt subjects all read it; no caller computes merge-base with main on its own
- application-architect: the baseline must also remember files that were untracked or dirty when the change opened, so pre-existing working-tree dirt is never counted as this change's edits
